claim_reviews.conclusion: Valid Indonesian expression for “lesson plan,” though “rencana pembelajaran” is often preferred in formal education contexts.
claim_reviews.subject: Indonesian: rencana pelajaran

claim_reviews.conclusion: Valid Malaysian Malay expression for a teacher’s lesson/teaching plan and well supported by Malaysian Ministry of Education usage.
claim_reviews.subject: Malaysian: rancangan pengajaran

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Lesson plan” and “teacher’s plan for a lesson” align with both Malay answers; the Malaysian form emphasizes teaching/instruction rather than the lesson as an object, without changing the intended sense.
claim_reviews.subject: English cue and sense

claim_reviews.conclusion: Appropriate as a broad learner-facing relation: the varieties use different conventional lexical choices, although the expressions are semantically equivalent.
claim_reviews.subject: Final relation: different-common-word

claim_reviews.conclusion: No genuine false-friend contrast is present. Indonesian rencana and Malaysian rancangan are cognate, closely synonymous words; pelajaran and pengajaran differ in aspect but remain transparently related in this educational phrase.
claim_reviews.subject: False-friend contrast

response.rationale: Both translations are semantically valid and attested. Indonesian also commonly uses the more institutional “rencana pembelajaran”/RPP, while Malaysian official usage strongly supports “rancangan pengajaran.” The forms differ lexically by national variety, but they are not false friends.
